A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ThinK, the same query-driven KV-cache channel-pruning work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the equations, tables, and figures can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original LongBench and Needle-in-a-Haystack experiments, channel-pruning ablations, and comparisons under equal cache-memory budgets.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds LLaMA-3-70B results, KIVI comparisons, and synthetic-workload peak-memory measurements.

M1.justification: The channel-selection objective, query-dependent score, observation window, and value-pruning rule remain unchanged. v2 Appendix C.1 adds a KIVI-specific inference procedure: pruning before quantization during prefill and pruning/quantizing accumulated decoding keys when the residual buffer reaches G tokens. The masked-query implementation illustrated in v2 was already described in v1.

E1.justification: LongBench and Needle-in-a-Haystack coverage remains unchanged. v2 Section 4.4 adds synthetic batched-generation workloads for peak-memory evaluation, providing a limited additional test scenario. The additional LLaMA backbones are changes in experimental configuration.

E2.justification: v2 extends the evaluated comparator families beyond token eviction by adding KIVI: Table 4 compares KIVI with KIVI plus ThinK, and Figure 3b includes 2-bit and 4-bit KIVI configurations. KIVI was cited but not experimentally compared in v1. H2O, SnapKV, and the magnitude-pruning comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds LLaMA-3-70B evaluations across cache budgets and LLaMA-2-7B-chat memory tests using 160-token inputs, 338-token outputs, varying batch sizes, and 2-bit/4-bit caches. These introduce substantial new configurations and peak-memory measurements. The magnitude-plot attribution also changes from LLaMA3-8B in v1 Figure 2 to LLaMA-2-7B in v2 Figure 4; this does not establish that the plot was regenerated.

E4.justification: v2 adds a batch-size sensitivity analysis of peak memory for KIVI with and without ThinK at two precisions, shown in Figure 3b. The recent-size, equal-memory, joint key/value-pruning, and retrieval-depth analyses are retained; their relocation or renumbering does not constitute new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests for its experiments. v2 continues the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All original table values are retained. v2 adds 70B results, including LongBench averages of 46.27 for SnapKV and 46.45 with ThinK at pruning ratio 0.4 and cache size 512. New Table 4 reports 31.92 for KIVI versus 31.77 with ThinK, while Figure 3b adds peak-memory curves. These are newly reported comparisons under additional configurations.

T1.justification: The pruning optimization, channel scores, selection constraints, SVD energy formula, and value-pruning equations are mathematically unchanged. The SVD formula and value-pruning formulation move to v2 Appendices A and D. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central channel-pruning novelty and memory-saving claims remain. v2 extends the headline empirical comparison to quantization and adds claims of 2.8-fold peak-memory reduction and up to fivefold batch capacity for ThinK combined with KIVI. Its contribution paragraph narrows the stated linear savings from both computation and memory to memory.

C2.justification: v2 removes v1 Section 3.3's argument that masked-query decoding should require less computation than zero-filling, and emphasizes the batch-capacity implications of the new KIVI measurements. Existing qualifications about aggressive pruning, small cache budgets, and value-cache pruning on Mistral remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 and Figure 7 newly document KIVI integration, including prefill ordering and residual-buffer handling. v2 also specifies the synthetic workload lengths and quantization precisions. It omits v1's zero-filling/FlashAttention implementation discussion and changes the hardware disclosure from one A100 to A100 GPUs without specifying their count.

R1.justification: v2 replaces the introductory Frankle–Carbin and Blalock pruning references with SparseGPT and Sun et al. (2023), adds mathematical-reasoning references, and removes Bordes et al. The principal positioning as channel pruning complementary to eviction and quantization remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 extensively edits the abstract, introduction, experimental discussion, related work, and conclusion. It removes the contents page, replaces 'End Note and Future Direction' with 'Conclusion', and reorganizes supporting material into Appendices A–D. These are substantial editorial and structural changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a substantially different, more compact layout. It expands Table 2 with 70B blocks, adds the KIVI table and workflow diagram, combines the existing equal-memory plot with a new memory-scaling panel, and redraws the decoding diagram. Magnitude plots, SVD plots, retrieval heatmaps, and the joint-pruning table move to appendices.

improvement.justification: v1 asserted compatibility with quantization without experimentally validating it. v2 supplies the KIVI accuracy comparison, peak-memory measurements across batch sizes, and an implementation description, substantially strengthening the practical compression claim. The 70B results also strengthen evidence beyond the original smaller models. Denser tables and incomplete KIVI configuration details limit readability and reproducibility, but do not outweigh these gains.
